steps.title: Import Vue and defineComponent
steps.instruction: Import Vue and defineComponent from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and defineComponent from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a module
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue and defineComponent APIs are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and defineComponent are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and defineComponent, which are essential for creating Vue components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and defineComponent from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import Vue and defineComponent from 'vue' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the TreeView component
steps.instruction: Create a default export component named TreeView using defineComponent.
steps.hint: Use defineComponent to define a Vue component with a name property set to 'TreeView'.
steps.seedCode:
import { defineComponent } from 'vue';

// Create a default export component named TreeView using defineComponent here
steps.expectedOutcome: A TreeView component is defined and ready to be built upon.
successCriteria: TreeView component is created as a default export using defineComponent with name property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TreeView component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using defineComponent and exporting it as default with the name 'TreeView'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using defineComponent and exporting it as default.

steps.title: Define props for tree data
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeView component, add a props object with a property named 'nodes' that accepts an array.
steps.hint: In Vue's defineComponent, you can define props as an object where each key is a prop name and the value is the expected type (like Array).
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeView component will be ready to receive tree data from a parent component through the 'nodes' prop.
successCriteria: The component has a props object with a 'nodes' property of type Array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the props for the TreeView component. Now it can receive tree data from its parent.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a props object with a 'nodes' property that accepts an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The props definition is missing or incorrect. The component needs a props object with a 'nodes' property of type Array.

steps.title: Initialize local state for expanded nodes
steps.instruction: Inside the component's setup function, create a reactive ref named 'expanded' initialized as an empty Set to store expanded node IDs.
steps.hint: Use Vue's ref function to create reactive state. Initialize it with new Set() to store unique IDs.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have reactive state to track which tree nodes are expanded.
successCriteria: A ref named 'expanded' is created inside setup() and initialized with new Set().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created reactive state to track expanded nodes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating a ref named 'expanded' and initializing it with new Set().
steps.feedbackWrong: The state wasn't set up correctly. You need to create a ref named 'expanded' inside the setup function.

steps.title: Create toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named toggleNode that takes a nodeId parameter. The function should toggle the presence of nodeId in the expanded Set.
steps.hint: Use the expanded.value Set's methods: .has() to check if a nodeId exists, .add() to include it, and .delete() to remove it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleNode function is defined that can add or remove node IDs from the expanded Set.
successCriteria: The toggleNode function is defined with a nodeId parameter and toggles the nodeId in the expanded Set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the toggle handler that will manage node expansion.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it properly toggles the nodeId in the expanded Set.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleNode function is missing or doesn't toggle the expanded Set correctly.

steps.title: Add template structure with v-if
steps.instruction: Add a template section to your component that uses v-if to check if nodes exist before rendering.
steps.hint: Remember to add a <template> tag and use the v-if directive with a condition that checks if nodes are present.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: conditional template structure
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template section with conditional rendering logic using v-if.
successCriteria: A template section is added with v-if directive that checks for nodes existence.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the template structure with v-if conditional rendering.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included the v-if directive properly in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure with v-if is missing or incorrect. Try adding a <template> section with v-if to check if nodes exist.

steps.title: Render tree nodes with v-for
steps.instruction: Inside the template's div, add a ul element with v-for to iterate through the nodes prop and render each node.
steps.hint: Use v-for="node in nodes" on the ul element to loop through the nodes array passed as a prop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: v-for to render list items
  • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes a ul element that will render each node from the nodes prop when the component is used with tree data.
successCriteria: A ul element with v-for="node in nodes" is added inside the div in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the v-for directive to iterate through the nodes. This will allow the component to render each tree node when provided with data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a ul element with v-for="node in nodes" inside the div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain a ul element with v-for="node in nodes" to iterate through the nodes prop.

steps.title: Add node content and toggle button
steps.instruction: Inside the v-for loop, add an li element that displays the node's label and a button to toggle expansion.
steps.hint: Use the node parameter from the v-for loop to access the label property. The button should call the toggleNode handler with the node's id.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying item content with interactive button
  • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template should include li elements that show node labels and toggle buttons for each node.
successCriteria: Each tree node displays its label text and has a button that calls toggleNode with the node's id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the node content display and interactive toggle buttons.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure each li contains both the node label display and a button that calls toggleNode with the node id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show node labels with toggle buttons. Add li elements inside the v-for loop to display each node's label and a toggle button.

steps.title: Wire toggle button to handler
steps.instruction: Add an @click event handler to the toggle button that calls the toggleNode function with the current node's id.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding click handler to a button
<button @click="handleClick(item.id)">Toggle</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggle button should have an @click event that triggers the toggleNode function with the node's id parameter.
successCriteria: The button element includes @click="toggleNode(node.id)" in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the toggle button to call the toggleNode handler with the node id.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an @click handler, but make sure it calls toggleNode with node.id as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle button needs an @click event handler that calls toggleNode with the node's id.

steps.title: Add recursive TreeView for child nodes
steps.instruction: Inside the existing v-if block for when the node has children and is expanded, add a recursive TreeView component that renders the node's children.
steps.hint: Use the TreeView component itself as a child element, passing the child nodes as props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeView component will now recursively render child nodes when a parent node is expanded.
successCriteria: TreeView component is used recursively inside the v-if block with proper props binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully implemented recursion by rendering TreeView within itself for child nodes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the TreeView component inside the v-if block and passing the child nodes as props.
steps.feedbackWrong: The recursive TreeView wasn't properly implemented. Check that you're using the TreeView component with the correct props binding.
